clue.text: .Depressed by autumn rain?

parts.note: something depressed has been pushed down
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Someone feeling low because of the wet weather of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' and 'autumn' look like mood and season, but they are the two pieces; 'rain' at the end, with its question mark, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a heavy shower or fall of precipitation.

clue.text: The person to approach with some affection

definitions.text: The person to approach with some affection

parts.words: The person to approach with some affection
parts.note: reads as someone to approach fondly, but affection is an old word for a disease or ailment, so it is whom you see when ill

explanation.definitionFit: A physician is the person you consult when suffering from an illness.

clue.text: A group of seamen grabbed by mate and put on guard

indicators.note: grabbed by says the first pieces are held inside the word for mate

parts.note: to wed is to marry, to mate
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A gang of sailors seized by a shipmate and made to stand watch.
explanation.walkthrough: A and RN go inside WED, after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: To be warned is to be alerted to danger and so made cautious.

clue.text: People role-playing it's the old old 'story!

parts.note: folk means people

indicators.note: playing suggests the word role taking on a different arrangement

explanation.surface: People acting parts in the same tale that has been told for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges ROLE into LORE; the stray quote mark is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore is the traditional tales and beliefs handed down through a community.

clue.text: Bound to provide grassland parking

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, poetic for grassland
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Obliged to supply a field for car parking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a jump or spring.

clue.text: A couple of renegades backed this fearsome woman

indicators.note: backed means the doubled word is read from the back, right to left
a couple of means two copies of the following word are used

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or renegade

explanation.surface: Two traitors back a formidable lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A couple of' doubles RAT to RATRAT, and 'backed' reverses that whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a person, often a woman, with a violent or formidable temper.

clue.text: Like many a worker, not upright

parts.note: as means like, in 'as good as gold'
L is 50 in Roman numerals, a large number
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Lots of workers are bent over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives L, Roman 50, a standard crossword stand-in for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slope, leaning at an angle.

clue.text: Hang over a number following earth-quake

indicators.note: following puts the number after the rearranged letters
quake means shake, so the letters of earth are shaken into a new order

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Ten more tremors come after an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quake' shakes EARTH into THREA, and TEN comes 'following' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten is to loom, as dark clouds hang over a scene.

clue.text: Spots the head's indiscretion

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A headmaster's pimples, an embarrassing lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is the geographical headland, not the body part or the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashness is acting without thought, a lack of prudence.

clue.text: Blue and thin after taking revolutionary cure

indicators.note: after places the word for thin behind the rearranged letters
revolutionary suggests turning things round, so the letters of the word cure are reordered

parts.note: lean means thin

explanation.surface: A feeble, pale patient after a radical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges CURE to CERU, and LEAN comes 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerulean is a deep sky-blue colour.

clue.text: Panics when a pupil prepares to do battle

parts.note: L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
to arm is to equip oneself for fighting

explanation.surface: A schoolchild gets ready to fight and everyone is alarmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarms, as a verb, means frightens or throws into panic, so it stands for panics as a plural noun too.

clue.text: Stick around longing for hot stuff

indicators.note: around says the word for stick goes outside the word for longing

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
a yen is a craving or longing

explanation.surface: Persevering in a craving for something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: CANE goes around YEN: CA, YEN, then NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper powder.

clue.text: Heartless people will go in alone quite blatantly

indicators.note: will go in says the piece from people is put inside the word for alone

parts.note: only means alone, as in 'only child'

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word people is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Unfeeling folk will enter by themselves without shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' leaves PE, the first and last letters of 'people', which 'will go in' ONLY after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly is doing it in plain view, without any concealment.

clue.text: A man in it may well get support

indicators.note: may well suggests the letters of a man in it welling up and stirring into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a well might get a helping hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'may well' rearranges the eight letters of A MAN IN IT; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a person is to keep them going, to provide for or uphold them.

clue.text: Concerned about coppers being critical

indicators.note: about says the word for concerned is wrapped round the coins

parts.note: caring means concerned for others
coppers are low-value coins, pence, P

explanation.surface: Worried about police officers who find fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' are not police but copper coins; P goes inside CARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping means finding fault in a petty, nagging way.

clue.text: The German is occupied by some paper, one imagines

indicators.note: is occupied by says the German word has another piece living inside it

parts.note: der is the German masculine definite article
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A German man buried in paperwork lets his mind drift.
explanation.walkthrough: REAM sits inside DER, between the D and the ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary who lets fancy run free is a person who imagines things.

clue.text: Disorder in the home's soon set straight

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A promise that the house will soon be tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'home's soon'; 'set straight' is surface dressing, telling the solver the letters run forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of untidiness or confusion.

clue.text: Bananas and biscuits

definitions.meaning: bananas is slang for mad, crazy

explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is British slang for insane, and also the plural of a dry savoury biscuit.

clue.text: Denied benefits assistance

parts.note: gains are benefits or advantages
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: Welfare payments and support refused.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests state welfare refused; 'benefits' and 'assistance' are simply synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny.

clue.text: Replaced stock in a bright colour

indicators.note: in places the word for stock inside the colour

parts.note: red is a bright colour
a store is a stock or supply

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper puts the goods back on the shelf in a vivid shade.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to put it back in place.

clue.text: Old foreign coin, the equivalent of about a pound

definitions.text: Old foreign coin, the equivalent of about a pound

parts.words: Old foreign coin, the equivalent of about a pound
parts.note: a descriptive definition of a former Spanish and Portuguese silver coin, given a rough value in sterling

explanation.definitionFit: The real was a silver coin of old Spain and Portugal, and is also the modern currency of Brazil.

clue.text: Making full use of the time that's left, the dog!

parts.note: a span is a stretch of time
i.e., short for id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone cramming the last moments with activity, then a cry of exasperation at the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is read as 'that is', abbreviated IE; 'Making full use of the' is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gundog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: Says a quarter should be put into trust perhaps

indicators.note: should be put into says the compass point is placed inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests the word trust in some other possible arrangement

parts.note: east, E, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Advice that a quarter of the money be placed in a trust fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TRUST to UTTRS, and E goes in before the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak or say aloud.

clue.text: Having business with Her Majesty, appears rather less relaxed

parts.note: a firm is a business
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stood for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone with royal business looks tenser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears rather' is linking material.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmer means more rigid or tense, the opposite of looser.

clue.text: A Quaker getting no back-up colours

parts.note: William Penn, founder of Pennsylvania, was a Quaker

indicators.note: back-up in a down clue means the word no is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A Quaker refuses to support a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'back-up' turns NO into ON beneath PENN.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours is a word for a flag or ensign; a pennon is a long narrow flag.

clue.text: Firm can't hold on to good man

indicators.note: hold says the word for can't contains the next pieces

parts.note: cant is the word can't without its apostrophe
taken as written
ST, saint, is the usual crossword good man

explanation.surface: A business that cannot keep its good employee.
explanation.walkthrough: CANT holds ON and ST: C, A, N then ON, ST, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means steadfast, unwavering.

clue.text: Priest forming a band

indicators.note: forming signals the letters of priest being shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A clergyman setting up a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow band of colour.

clue.text: A Greek character given a little bribe takes extra care

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A Greek character given a little bribe takes extra care' (4) for BETA: B plus ETA uses 'A Greek character' both as definition and as ETA, and 'takes extra care' has no job; the clue looks garbled and no search gives the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: A Greek character given a little bribe takes extra care

clue.text: Fellow in' shelter returning for a top-coat

indicators.note: returning means the assembled piece is read backwards
in places the word for fellow inside the word for shelter

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man coming back into a shelter to fetch his overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN goes 'in' LEE to make LEMANE, which 'returning' turns round. The stray apostrophe after 'in' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard glossy paint or finishing coat applied on top.

clue.text: An offer of a little money would make him cross with one!

definitions.text: An offer of a little money would make him cross with one!

parts.words: An offer of a little money would make him cross with one!
parts.note: reads as someone annoyed by a stingy tip, but describes the boatman paid a coin to carry a passenger over water, as Charon was paid by the dead

explanation.definitionFit: A boatman who carries passengers over a river charges a fare for each crossing.

clue.text: The evil individual is put down first

parts.note: down means sad, low in spirits
first is written 1st, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A villain is humbled at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'first' as 1ST, with the digit standing for I; 'is put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist is a cruel person who enjoys inflicting pain on others.

clue.text: An influential Oriental, and treated right when in deep water

indicators.note: when in says the other pieces are placed inside the word for deep water

parts.note: the main is the open sea

indicators.note: treated suggests the word and being processed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A powerful Chinese official, roughly handled and adrift at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' turns AND into NDA; add R and put the four letters inside MAIN after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a high-ranking official of imperial China, hence any powerful bureaucrat.
